messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prod-inference-high-errors triggered by error-rate > 5% across canary pool for model-rev: r2025-03-14-quant. Incident ID: INC-20250315-001
Maya: I'm on it — picking up the page. Briefing: canary traffic (5% sample) started rolling at 14:05 UTC. Error spike started ~14:10.
Jon: joining. Observed increased 500s and some tokenization errors in logs.
Sasha: seeing customer-facing latencies for a few VIP customers in logs (webhook timeouts). Not widespread but hitting a few high-traffic routes.
Derek: timeline question — did we change the routing policy or batching config with this rollout?
Maya: no routing changes. Canary used default batching. Model diff: base r2025-03-10 vs canary r2025-03-14-quant (smaller, quantized).
Jon: pasting grep of error snippets:
```
2025-03-15T14:09:58Z [serving] ERROR request_id=abc123 model=r2025-03-14-quant tokenization: unsupported byte seq
2025-03-15T14:10:03Z [worker-7] 500 POST /v1/generate host=api.redwood/ model=r2025-03-14-quant err=kvcache-mismatch
2025-03-15T14:11:15Z [router] WARN fallback-trigger model=r2025-03-14-quant latency=1200ms
```
Maya: thanks. Hypothesis A: quantization introduced tokenization mismatch for some unicode sequences. Hypothesis B: KV cache layout change causing mismatched cache leading to 500s under concurrency.
Sasha: correlation with Unicode-heavy prompts from two customers — I pulled sample requests.
Eva: adding customer impact: two paying customers (acct: AcmeCorp, acct: BrightAds) saw 100-200 failed requests per minute between 14:10-14:22 UTC. No data loss layer reported yet.
Kevin: quick check — can we pin those customers to last-known-good model while we investigate? That would mitigate impact.
Maya: yes. Oncall runbook step: pin-routing for specific customer IDs to model r2025-03-10. Doing patch now.
ops-bot: command executed: `patch-routing --customer AcmeCorp --model r2025-03-10 --force` -> success
ops-bot: command executed: `patch-routing --customer BrightAds --model r2025-03-10 --force` -> success
Jon: telemetry after pinning: error-rate for those accounts dropped to baseline within 90s. Good mitigation.
Derek: can we temporarily stop canary rollout to prevent further exposure?
Maya: stopping canary flag now. `canary-controller pause --rollout canary-2025-03-14-quant`
ops-bot: command queued -> success. Traffic for new sessions will no longer be assigned to the canary.
Sasha: capturing a short timeline to seed RCA:
- 14:05 UTC: Canary rollout r2025-03-14-quant (5% sample) begins
- 14:09-14:11 UTC: Error spike detected in canary pool, first 500s
- 14:12 UTC: Pager triggered, Maya paged
- 14:13-14:16 UTC: Oncall triage + gather logs
- 14:17 UTC: Pinning VIP customers to r2025-03-10
- 14:19 UTC: Canary paused
- 14:22 UTC: Error rates for pinned customers returned to baseline
- 14:35 UTC: Continued investigation into tokenization + kvcache mismatch
Jon: sharing diff from model packaging step (snippet):
```
- tokenizer.json v1.4 checksum: abcdef
+ tokenizer.json v1.5 checksum: abcdff  <-- different normalizer behavior
- kv-layout: v2
+ kv-layout: v2-quant-compact
```
Maya: important: packaging notes show quantized build used smaller KV layout which required different cache alignment. If mis-declared, some workers may treat KV offsets incorrectly.
Derek: can we reproduce locally with stress harness? I'll run replay of the failing requests with unicode payloads and concurrent runs.
Jon: running local replay now; capturing logs to /tmp/replay-1804501120.log. Expect ~5-10m.
Eva: customer comms: I drafted a short message to affected customers acknowledging impact and mitigation. Will post once we confirm root cause.
Maya: Decision matrix for next steps in-thread:
- Rollback canary entirely -> Low cost since only 5% but stops further exposure.
- Pin versions for VIP only -> partial mitigation (we did this).
- Patch tokenizer or KV handling in quantized runtime -> will require build/test and deploy (longer).
- Re-run canary with stricter validation and sample of unicode-heavy prompts -> medium term.
Sasha: given immediate customer impact, recommend rollback full canary to avoid accidental leak to other accounts while we debug.
Maya: agree. Executing rollback to r2025-03-10 for canary group.
ops-bot: command executed: `canary-controller rollback --rollout canary-2025-03-14-quant --to r2025-03-10` -> success
Jon: monitoring error-rate cluster-wide — dropping now from 4.8% to 0.6% over next ~2 minutes.
Derek: logging checklist to capture for RCA: all request traces for 14:05-14:25, worker kernel traces for quantized commit, packaging checksums, own replay logs.
Maya: I'll create a shared S3 artifact bundle: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20250315-001/artifacts/ (will upload logs + diffs).
Maya: Uploaded artifacts:
- /artifacts/logs/replay-1804501120.log
- /artifacts/packaging/diff-tokenizer-kv.txt
- /artifacts/metrics/errored-requests-14-05-14-25.csv
Jon: preliminary root cause hypothesis for RCA: packaging introduced tokenizer normalizer change + kv-layout change with insufficient validation for edge-case unicode sequences under quantized runtime, leading to tokenization failures and KV cache mismatch under concurrency -> 500s.
Sasha: action items assigned in-thread:
- Jon: provide detailed repro and unit test for unicode tokenizer edge-cases (ETA: 24h)
- Derek: add KV-layout validation to serving runtime (ETA: 48h)
- Maya: follow-up postmortem doc + timeline (ETA: 48h)
- Eva: customer follow-ups + post-incident notes (ETA: today EOD)
- Kevin: add canary gating checks for tokenizer checksum and a small unicode test set to pre-rollout CI (ETA: 72h)
Maya: tagging for RCA writeup: include diff artifacts, timeline, decision to rollback, mitigation steps (pinning + rollback), and customer impact summary.
Jon: adding a quick reproducible command we used:
```
replayer --model r2025-03-14-quant --trace --payload samples/unicode-heavy.json --concurrency 12 > /tmp/replay-1804501120.log
```
Derek: note for postmortem: check whether autoscaling led to mixing of old/new runtime worker binaries in the same pool during canary (race condition).
Maya: thanks all. Closing immediate on-call loop — services back to baseline, customers mitigated. We will continue RCA in incident doc. If anyone has extra logs or traces drop them into s3 path above.
Eva: posting customer notes now.
ops-bot: incident INC-20250315-001 status -> mitigated (rollback + customer pin).
Maya: moving to follow-up channel: /incident-postmortems/INC-20250315-001. Please subscribe for the RCA draft.
Kevin: quick reminder: add a canary gating item to block quantized builds unless tokenizer checksum is identical to non-quantized baseline or passes unicode smoke tests.
Jon: ack. I'll start a PR with unit tests.
Sasha: nice work team. :thumbsup:
Maya: end of thread for oncall. We'll carry forward to postmortem doc.
